chunks: Rubayʿ ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام gave as charity his house that was in al-Madīnah among Banī Zurayq, and he wrote:
In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.
This is what ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib gave in charity while he was alive and sound: he gave his house in Banī Zurayq as a charity that is neither to be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited.
Until Allah, Who inherits the heavens and the earth, inherits it.
And he settled his maternal aunts in this charity for as long as they lived and their descendants remained; then when they pass away, it shall belong to the needy among the Muslims.

key_terms.لَا تُبَاعُ: it is not to be sold
key_terms.لَا تُورَثُ: it is not to be inherited as ordinary property
key_terms.لَا تُوهَبُ: it is not to be gifted away

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام designate his house in Banī Zurayq as a perpetual charity?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written charitable endowment by Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام concerning his house in Banī Zurayq. It establishes that the property was to remain a perpetual charity, reserved first for the residence of his maternal aunts and their descendants, and afterward for needy Muslims.
